When we talk about personal income in the context of BEA’s economic statistics, however, it’s my paycheck, your paycheck, your cousin’s paycheck—and much more. In fact, I believe our monthly personal income statistics are the most comprehensive measure of U.S. economic activity available on a monthly basis. They are also a widely used tool for analyzing consumer purchasing power. What is personal income? It’s income that people get from wages and salaries, Social Security and other government benefits, dividends and interest, business ownership, and other sources. Not only do we produce monthly estimates for the entire country, but we also produce quarterly estimates of personal income for individual states , and annual estimates down to the level of counties . We even have annual estimates of the distribution of personal income to households. It turns out that we’ve been publishing personal income statistics for a long time. The origin and evolution of these statistics are, for me, a textbook example of listening and responding to the needs of customers. If you’re lucky, you might even get to see one. Even if you don't, you’ll never be far from one, because this is bear country! Brown bears like the wide-open tundra while black bears prefer the forest, although they will sometimes venture out onto the tundra in search of food. Even though Kobuk Valley is in the Arctic, there are no polar bears here. Polar bears live on the sea ice and don't venture this far inland. The river flows west past the jagged limestone ridges of the White Mountains before flowing to the north and east, where it enters the Yukon Flats and joins the Yukon River. Beaver Creek has long been a popular destination for river adventurers. The river's clear water, modest Class I rapids, and unparalleled scenery make for a relaxing trip. Once you put in at Nome Creek, there are no roads or services until you reach the Yukon River bridge on the Dalton Highway. Many floaters arrange for a Fairbanks air-taxi service to pick them up from a gravel bar. Check with the air-taxis for current information on suitable pickup locations. Once they enter the any colony, the beetles can never leave. Sceptobius beetles are seen grooming an ant as part of their evolved symbiotic relationship. D. Miller, Parker Lab/Caltech By Jason Bittel Published February 5, 2026 Life may look like a paradise for beetles living in ant colonies. Plump, wriggling ant larvae and helpless eggs sit waiting to be devoured, while hundreds of thousands of ants stand at the ready to ward off predators and parasites. There’s just one catch for these beetles, revealed in a new study published in the journal Cell . If one leaves the ant colony, it’ll be dead in less than a day. From bacteria living inside insect guts to mycorrhizal fungi on plant roots, symbiotic organisms abound across the tree of life, says Joseph Parker , an evolutionary biologist at the California Institute of Technology and senior author of the study. All these symbiotes have something in common that can also be a liability—their evolutionary entwinement has progressed so far, they can no longer live without their hosts. Parker and his colleagues wanted to know why. They tackled this question by investigating the odd relationship between a rove beetle known as Sceptobius lativentris and its host, the velvety tree ant. pages.text: Before Mountain Biking Became One of the Most Popular Recreational Sports, Adventurous Souls of the American West Had to Invent a Rugged Bike Skip to main content Breeze’s earlier conceptual drawing for the Breezer 1 prototype. In the 1960s and ’70s, a countercultural movement drew a new generation of pioneers to the West. Suddenly, ski bums, scofflaws, draft dodgers and hippie homesteaders were joining the miners and hardscrabble farmers of mountain towns like Crested Butte, Colorado. Looking for a way to navigate both the Pontiac-bedeviling potholes in town as well as the dirt roads leading into the mountains, a small crew of Crested Butte transplants began building handmade off-road-ready bikes. They used a hodgepodge of vintage parts, in particular from World War II-era Schwinn bicycles. The group called itself the Grubstake Gang (named after a favorite watering hole), and they rejoiced when their heavy cruisers, outfitted with fat tires, proved capable of handling the punishing unpaved roads into and out of town. In September 1976, 15 cyclists attempted a seemingly impossible feat: riding these “klunkers” over 12,700-foot Pearl Pass to Aspen. The next day, just two riders rolled into Aspen; the steep Colorado stones of the 38-mile road had destroyed all the other klunkers. Around the same time, a group of teenagers in California’s Marin County—they called themselves the Larkspur Canyon Gang —were tinkering and racing their own garage-built bikes down the steep roads of Mount Tamalpais , north of San Francisco. Read on to discover more about this little book and the fascinating origins of many of our beloved nursery rhymes. 13 November 2026 Blog series English and Drama Author Maddy Smith, Lead Curator of Printed Heritage Collections (1601-1900) Have you ever wondered where nursery rhymes like 'hush-a-bye baby', 'hickery dickery dock', 'baa baa black sheep' and 'Jack and Gill went up the hill' came from? Well, it's World Nursery Rhyme Week and the British Library has recently acquired for the nation an exceptionally rare copy of Mother Goose's Melody: or, Sonnets for the Cradle printed in 1791. This is a little children's book full of rhymes, humour and entertaining woodcut illustrations, and it contains the first recorded appearance in print of many nursery rhymes still familiar to us today. It is one of the most important collections of nursery rhymes ever published in Britain. Many later editions of traditional nursery rhymes in Britain and North America were based on rhymes in Mother Goose's Melody. Even Arkansans have largely forgotten that this attractive spa town was America’s original Sin City, teeming with casinos and brothels, and frequented by big-name gangsters. The mobster Bugsy Siegel may have even used Hot Springs as an inspiration when he was developing the Las Vegas Strip. The leading authority on the town’s colorful, decadent, sinful history (it was known as “the loose buckle in the Bible Belt”) is a charismatic, white-haired, sharp-dressed man named Robert K. Raines. A former rock singer and computer salesman, he has written a book and made several short documentaries about vice and organized crime in Hot Springs. pages.text: Ben Franklin Wasn’t Serious When He Implied the Wild Turkey Would Be a ‘Respectable’ National Symbol … but He Wasn’t Wrong, Either Skip to main content The head of a male turkey is distinguished by the colorful dewlap and caruncles on its neck. Joanna Lentini The wild turkey is a noble beast: the muscular, bronze-sheened ancestor of the barnyard turkeys we eat today. While the two technically belong to the same species, the barnyard variety is relatively new on the scene. People began domesticating wild turkeys in what is now Mexico more than 2,000 years ago, selectively breeding them over generations to become fat and docile. Wild turkeys, meanwhile, have inhabited North America for a much longer time—hundreds of thousands of years. Hunters still eat them, of course, and appreciate the lean gaminess of the wild flesh. But for most of us, the bird is less about sustenance than about a glimpse of the true national temperament: resourceful and restless, by turns noble and idiotic—as liable to swagger into view as to bolt for the trees. This feathery American character has long invited comparison with another native bird. When the Continental Congress first chose the bald eagle for our fledgling nation’s heraldry, Benjamin Franklin wrote to his daughter in 1784 condemning it as “a bird of bad moral character,” given to stealing food from smaller birds rather than hunting for itself. pages.description: Midfielder Declan Rice has defended his Arsenal team-mate Ben White after he was booed during England's win over Croatia at Wembley.
pages.text: Ben White: Declan Rice defends Arsenal team-mate after boos at Wembley - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Declan Rice joined Ben White at Arsenal after signing from West Ham in 2023 Published 14 November 2026 Declan Rice has defended Arsenal team-mate Ben White after the defender was booed at Wembley during England's 2-1 win over Croatia on Thursday. White, who came on as a substitute in the Nations League fixture, left the Three Lions' camp at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar to return home for personal reasons. He then made himself unavailable for selection for the rest of Gareth Southgate's reign. White was also booed by some fans in March's 1-1 draw with Ukraine after returning to the squad under Thomas Tuchel. "The incident with Ben was over five years ago, I don't know why it is still a conversation to be honest," Rice told BBC Radio 5 Live. "Knowing Ben, knowing the character he is, he has totally moved on from all of that. "He always wears the shirt with pride and every time he puts on the shirt, he gives 100 percent. "It shows his character. It is not easy being booed coming on at Wembley, but to show his mental strength to play the game and to play well, like he did in the previous months, is a real testament to him." Rice also said that the players do not discuss the situation at all and that everybody has moved on, adding that White has "an exciting future ahead with this England squad". Home Menu About Documentation Download License Support Purchase Search About Documentation Download Support Purchase Search Documentation Search Changelog SQLite As An Application File Format (Note: The current page is a brief summary of why SQLite makes a good application file format. The topic is considered at greater detail in a separate technical note .) SQLite has been used with great success as the on-disk file format for desktop applications such as version control systems, financial analysis tools, media cataloging and editing suites, CAD packages, record keeping programs, and so forth. The traditional File/Open operation calls sqlite3_open() to attach to the database file. Updates happen automatically as application content is revised so the File/Save menu option becomes superfluous. The File/Save_As menu option can be implemented using the backup API . There are many advantages to using SQLite as an application file format, including: Better performance Reading and writing from an SQLite database is often faster than reading and writing individual files from disk. See 35% Faster Than The Filesystem and Internal Versus External BLOBs . The application only has to load the data it needs, rather than reading the entire file and holding a complete parse in memory. Small edits only overwrite the parts of the file that change, reducing write time and wear on SSD drives. Reduced application cost and complexity No application file I/O code to write and debug. West was born in Swarthmore, Pennsylvania, in 1738, when the American colonies were still part of the British Empire, and became an renowned history painter and the second president of England’s Royal Academy of Arts. While in London, West befriended Franklin, a fellow Pennsylvanian, but did not render this likeness of the celebrated scientist and American statesman until after his death, creating it as a study for a larger, unrealized portrait that he planned to give to Pennsylvania Hospital, an institution Franklin founded in Philadelphia. pages.text: Bernardino Luini (about 1480 - 1532) | National Gallery, London Skip to main content Luini was the most famous Milanese painter of the early 16th century. He worked as a fresco painter in Milan, and also in Saronno and Lugarno and elsewhere in Lombardy. Luini was deeply affected by Leonardo da Vinci , who was in Milan from 1483. Many of his paintings, like 'Christ among the Doctors' and the 'Virgin and Child with Saint John' derive from Leonardo compositions. Luini also adopted Leonardo's use of chiaroscuro , and his facial types. As a fresco painter, Luini worked in a style which was influenced by the 15th-century Lombard tradition and particularly by Foppa . In panel painting, Luini transcribed Leonardo's compositions with competence, but he lacked the subtlety of Leonardo's own approach. Leonardo's repertoire of figures and chiaroscuro are combined in the work of Luini with the harsher Lombard style that influenced his fresco paintings.
